stanzas: 저기 저 산 밑에 도라지가 한들한들
orig.credit: Traditional; the Korean text as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: white doraji of the deep, deep mountains and streams:
though I dig up only one or two roots,
they fill a bamboo basket half full [?].
Down there at the foot of that mountain the doraji sway and sway.
white doraji of Geumsanpo in Eunyul:
one root, two roots I take up [?],
it is a rich year for doraji in the mountain valley.
white doraji of Geumgangsan in Gangwon-do:
how fine is the skill of their hands!
jeogi jeo san mite dorajiga handeulhandeul
rom.credit: Romanization: The Epoch Institute (Revised Romanization of Korean)

notes: doraji is the balloon flower (Platycodon grandiflorus), whose root is dug and eaten; kept as the song's word throughout.
line 1.4: 'bansil' is not standard Korean; read here as 'half full' (ban, half). The sense, a basket filled by only one or two roots, is a picture of plenty.
lines 2.1 and 2.2: 'eheyo', 'ehaeya' and 'eoyeorananda' are sung syllables with no fixed meaning, kept as syllables; 'jihwaja' is a cheer of delight.
line 3.2: Eunyul is a county in Hwanghae Province; Geumsanpo a place there.
line 3.3: 'badeuni', literally 'as (I) receive'; the sense here may be 'as I gather them'.
line 4.2: Geumgangsan, the Diamond Mountains, in Gangwon Province.
